definition: a filmmaker whose personal style dominates their work
memoryTip: French “author” of film — director as personal style signature.
correctPassage: Critics treated the director as an auteur whose vision defined every frame.
wrongPassages: The stand looked auteur at dawn before any vendor unlocked a stall.
The quay looked auteur when containers stacked above the crane line.
The panel issued an auteur finding that restated the charge without deciding it.

definition: confuse; make muddy or unclear
memoryTip: Be-muddle: make muddy and confused.
correctPassage: Too many conflicting instructions only bemuddle new volunteers.
wrongPassages: The glacier walk felt bemuddle on a rubber-mat path with railings.
Her bemuddle attachment list named exhibits never filed with the court.
The lab hoped to bemuddle turnaround by auto-releasing unreviewed results.

definition: fleeting; lasting only a short time
memoryTip: Fugue/flee — flees quickly; fleeting.
correctPassage: Fame in that industry is fugacious, lasting only until the next trend.
wrongPassages: Audiences called the remix film fugacious for replacing the original score entirely.
The névé bench felt fugacious on a summer path of rubber mats.
The tonic pedal was fugacious under a coda in a foreign key.

definition: very typical of a certain kind
memoryTip: Archetype classic — the original mold of a type.
correctPassage: The story follows an archetypal journey from innocence to experience.
wrongPassages: The salt pan stayed archetypal in a climate file with no wet season.
Committees dropped the archetypal meal delivery homebound clients still used.
His archetypal request for admission asked parties to admit the sky is blue.

definition: the most perfect example of a quality
memoryTip: Fifth essence (perfect core) — purest example.
correctPassage: The café is the quintessential neighborhood hangout.
wrongPassages: The quay’s quintessential wind sock hung limp under a painted breeze.
He filed the incident as quintessential though cameras showed a clear sequence.
a quintessential crowd of two people was written up as a sold-out premiere.

definition: the state of lasting only a short time
memoryTip: Transient = temporary — short-lived nature.
correctPassage: The installation emphasizes the transience of digital memory.
wrongPassages: The lost battery in bin transience corroded a binder clip black.
He toggled transience and only the cursor theme changed.
She spray-marked the cask transience and packed spare nozzles.

definition: unfair bias; a particular liking
memoryTip: Partial to one side — unfair bias (or a soft spot).
correctPassage: Reviewers must avoid partiality toward authors they know personally.
wrongPassages: The recipe’s partiality was “about a cup,” printed as if it were a precise unit.
The camping shelf’s partiality sat beside fuel canisters and a bent spoon.
The museum’s partiality drawer held screws, washers, and one unlabeled key.

definition: difficult to accept or find pleasant
memoryTip: Can’t palate it — hard to swallow, unpleasant truth.
correctPassage: The report contains unpalatable truths about the project’s cost overruns.
wrongPassages: The organ point was unpalatable after the choir cadenced without it.
an unpalatable characterization test freezes a known bug as correct behavior.
The depot’s unpalatable arrivals board listed trains from a closed branch line.

definition: produce and discharge a substance; or hide away
memoryTip: Secret-e: hide away, or glands secrete fluids.
correctPassage: Certain glands secrete hormones that regulate metabolism.
wrongPassages: The mediant held was secrete under a final cadence that never used III.
The path felt secrete under ice groomed flat for racing.
The fen pool stayed secrete after the catch drain ran dry all summer.

definition: a condition that limits a statement; or a credential
memoryTip: A qualifying limit or a credential — softens a claim / certifies you.
correctPassage: She accepted the praise with one important qualification.
wrongPassages: She measured “one qualification” of flour as whatever fit the mug.
She labeled the locker qualification and left a single unmatched glove inside.
The folder qualification held only a desktop.ini and dust.

definition: careful thought; or something given in exchange
memoryTip: Careful thought — or something given in a deal.
correctPassage: After careful consideration, the board rejected the merger.
wrongPassages: The ribbon for consideration said “thanks for coming” on the back.
She painted the drum consideration and stored festival maps from last year.
Sharps took the corroded clip that had lived in bin consideration.

definition: marked by decline or luxurious self-indulgence
memoryTip: De-cadence: falling from standards — luxuriously self-indulgent decline.
correctPassage: Critics called the late period’s art decadent and self-indulgent.
wrongPassages: a decadent DR test is a calendar invite nobody accepts.
Trustees denied the decadent language-access line interpreters needed daily.
Her decadent notice to produce sought devices no party ever possessed.

definition: put at risk of harm
memoryTip: In peril — put at risk.
correctPassage: Rising seas have imperiled several coastal archaeological sites.
wrongPassages: They tried to imperiled the sinkhole by installing a decorative fence around it.
She hoped to imperiled the debt by charging interest to the same unpaid balance.
To imperiled the experiment, the team simply powered down and left for lunch.

definition: playfully dishonest or mischievous
memoryTip: Like a charming rogue — playfully mischievous.
correctPassage: A roguish smile suggested he was not entirely serious.
wrongPassages: The leading tone held was roguish under a final chord on VI.
She marked the dependency roguish after deleting the only import that used it.
The limit switch was roguish and sat past the mechanical stop.

definition: relating to a roguish hero's episodic adventures
memoryTip: Picaro = rogue hero — episodic adventures of a rascal.
correctPassage: The novel is picaresque: a string of adventures with a clever outsider at its center.
wrongPassages: Fans found the spatial mix picaresque for parking vocals outside the screen.
The fuse rating was picaresque and never protected the circuit it named.
The snow shelf felt picaresque after a deck and railing were installed.

definition: change direction when passing through a medium
memoryTip: Re-fract light: bend it as it passes through glass/water.
correctPassage: A prism will refract white light into a spectrum of colors.
wrongPassages: a refract exercise AAR is “went fine” with no metrics attached.
The moss pool stayed refract when the ditch network dried the mire.
Teachers called the unit refract after students taught the final lesson themselves.

definition: standard or commonly used (as in a stock response)
memoryTip: Off-the-shelf stock answer — standard, not original.
correctPassage: He answered with a stock phrase that revealed little of his real view.
wrongPassages: a stock canary deploy ships to zero users and declares success.
a stock DR proof is a screenshot of a green dashboard from last year.
The memo was stock: a subject line only and an empty body.

definition: a sudden invasion or attack
memoryTip: In-curse of attack — sudden invasion into territory.
correctPassage: A brief military incursion raised tensions along the border.
wrongPassages: She used incursion as a filename for an empty document on the desktop.
He retagged the orphan keys incursion and still could not match a lock.
Daylight still could not separate Incursion Sand from Putty on the fan deck.

definition: give or enhance the value or status of
memoryTip: Valor + ize: give value/status to something.
correctPassage: The museum seeks to valorize craft traditions long treated as minor arts.
wrongPassages: They tried to valorize the erosion by installing cameras instead of shoring.
He moved to valorize the subpoena by blaming a former intern for the account.
He tried to valorize the stain with the solvent that set it permanently.

definition: destroy a large proportion of
memoryTip: Originally kill every tenth; now destroy a large share.
correctPassage: Disease can decimate a population that has no prior immunity.
wrongPassages: The policy will decimate staffing by adding twenty percent more positions.
Gentle rain decimated the garden by making every plant greener overnight.
They decimated the archive by digitizing and preserving every page with care.
